drivingQuestion: Does the mishna imply the flayer burns the parts himself?
outcomeNote: Resolved by rereading the mishna's wording.

segments.he: כֵּיצַד תּוֹלִין וּמַפְשִׁיטִין וְכוּ׳. קְרָעוֹ, וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת אֵמוּרָיו. נְתָנָם בְּמָגֵיס לְהַקְטִירָם. אַטּוּ הוּא גּוּפֵיהּ הֲוָה מַקְטַר לְהוּ? אֵימָא: לְהַקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
segments.en: It was taught in the mishna «how one would suspend and flay» the Paschal lamb, and that after the flaying «he would tear it» open and «remove its sacrificial parts» and then «place them in a large basin in order to burn them.» The Gemara asks: «Is that to say that he himself,» the priest who placed the sacrificial parts in the basin and no one else, «would burn them?» The Gemara answers: Correct the wording of the mishna to «say: In order to burn them on the altar,» meaning that he would place them in a large basin as preparation for their being burned on the altar, but not that he himself would necessarily burn them.
